question: In badminton, a ________ is called when a rally is stopped without any point.
solution:
The correct answer is __**let**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A "let" in badminton occurs when a rally is stopped and replayed without any point being awarded.
 
• It is commonly called when an unforeseen or accidental event disrupts the play, such as the shuttlecock getting stuck in the net.
 
• Situations like server serving before the receiver is ready or double faults also result in a "let".
 
• The referee or umpire has the authority to call a "let" during a match.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rally**

 
 
• A rally is a sequence of back-and-forth shots between players, started by a serve.
 
• The rally continues until the shuttlecock hits the ground, goes out of bounds, or a fault is committed.
 
 
 
• **Faults**
 
 
• A fault is any violation of the rules resulting in the loss of service or point.
 
• Common faults include touching the net with the racket, hitting the shuttlecock out of bounds, and not serving correctly.
 
 
 
• **Serve**
 
 
• Serving is how the game is started and how each rally begins.
 
• The serve must be performed underhand and the server must hit the shuttlecock below the waist.
 
 
 
• **Scoring System**
 
 
• A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points.
 
• Every time there is a serve, there is a point scored.
 
• The side winning a rally adds a point to its score.
